items.title: The Myth of Multitasking
items.text: Many people proudly say they are good at multitasking. However, studies show that the brain does not really do two things at once. It switches quickly from one task to another, and every switch costs a little time and attention. A student who answers messages while reading a textbook usually needs longer to finish and remembers less afterward. Instead of handling everything together, it is wiser to give one job your full attention, complete it, and then move on. In other words, the best way to work faster is to ______.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Students who send messages are better at remembering information.
The brain becomes stronger when it handles many jobs at once.
Doing tasks one by one is more effective than doing them together.
People who say they multitask are usually telling a lie to others.
qs.why: However 뒤에 통념(멀티태스킹)을 뒤집고 마지막 문장에서 한 번에 하나씩 하라고 정리해요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: concentrate on a single task at a time
add more tasks to the same hour
switch between jobs as often as possible
check new messages after every page
qs.why: 앞 내용 전체를 요약하는 결론이므로, 한 가지에 집중하라는 말이 와야 해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what happens when a student reads while answering messages?
o: The student finishes the reading earlier than usual.
The student pays closer attention to the book.
The student switches tasks without losing any time.
The student remembers less of the text.
qs.why: 'needs longer to finish and remembers less afterward'가 근거예요.

qs.q: In the passage, the phrase “costs a little time” is closest in meaning to
o: saves quite a bit of time
uses up some time
asks for money
gives extra time
qs.why: 여기서 cost는 '(시간 등을) 들게 하다, 잃게 하다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Why We Yawn Together
items.text: Yawning looks simple, yet scientists still argue about why we do it. One old idea says that a yawn brings extra oxygen to the body, but experiments have not supported this. A newer idea is that yawning cools the brain, which would explain why people yawn more when the air is warm. Even more puzzling is that yawns spread from person to person. Watching someone yawn can make you do it too, and the effect is stronger among close friends and family members than among strangers. Some researchers therefore suspect that shared yawning has more to do with empathy than with tiredness.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Warm weather is the true cause of tiredness.
The reasons for yawning are still being debated.
Strangers yawn together more often than family members do.
Oxygen is the only thing the brain needs.
qs.why: 여러 가설을 소개하며 아직 논쟁 중이라고 말해요.

qs.q: Which idea about yawning has NOT been supported by experiments?
o: A yawn may help to cool the brain.
Yawns can spread between people.
Close friends yawn together more often.
A yawn gives the body extra oxygen.
qs.why: 첫 번째 가설만 'experiments have not supported this'라고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the last sentence?
o: Yawning together may reflect emotional closeness.
People yawn only when they are alone and tired.
Researchers have already proved that empathy causes yawns.
Yawning is more common in strangers than in relatives.
qs.why: 마지막 문장은 하품의 전염이 피로보다 공감과 더 관련 있을 수 있다고 추측해요. 'suspect'이므로 증명된 것은 아니에요.

qs.q: The word “puzzling” in the passage means
o: easy to see
pleasant to hear
hard to explain
quick to finish
qs.why: puzzling은 '이해하거나 설명하기 어려운'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: A Town Without Cars
items.text: When the city of Rivermouth closed its main street to traffic, many shop owners were afraid that customers would stay away. The first month was indeed quiet. But slowly, families began to walk through the area, cafés placed tables on the old road, and street musicians arrived. After a year, the shops reported higher sales than before. Fewer cars meant less noise and cleaner air, and people were willing to spend more time outside. The experience shows that a change that looks like a loss at first can ______ in the long run.

qs.q: Which phrase best fills the blank?
o: become an even bigger problem
lead to fewer customers
stay exactly the same
turn out to be a benefit
qs.why: 처음엔 걱정했지만 1년 후 매출이 늘었다는 흐름이므로 '이득이 되다'가 맞아요.

qs.q: What is the best title for the passage?
o: Why Shop Owners Dislike Musicians
How Closing a Road Helped a Town
The Dangers of Walking Downtown
A Year of Noisy Streets in Rivermouth
qs.why: 차 없는 거리 조성이 결과적으로 도움이 되었다는 것이 글의 요지예요.

qs.q: What happened in the first month after the road was closed?
o: Sales were already higher.
Musicians left the town.
Business was slow.
Cafés were forced to close.
qs.why: 'The first month was indeed quiet.'가 근거예요.

qs.q: Which of the following is suggested by the passage?
o: The early fears turned out to be mistaken.
Most customers drove to the street every day.
Cleaner air made people stop shopping.
The city planned to reopen the road to cars.
qs.why: 처음의 걱정과 달리 매출이 올랐다는 점에서 추론할 수 있어요.

items.title: Learning from Mistakes
items.text: Most of us feel embarrassed when we get something wrong, so we try to hide our mistakes. Yet a famous teacher once told her class, “A day without an error is a day without learning.” She did not mean that mistakes are enjoyable. She meant that an error shows exactly where our understanding stops. A student who gets a math problem wrong can look at each step and find the weak point, but a student who always chooses easy problems never discovers any weak point at all. For this reason, mistakes should be treated as information, not as proof that we are not clever.

qs.q: Which statement best expresses the writer's main idea?
o: Errors give us useful information for improving.
Easy problems are better for a student's confidence.
Teachers should avoid pointing out wrong answers.
A clever person never makes a mistake in class.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 실수를 증명이 아니라 정보로 보라고 정리해요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention a student who always chooses easy problems?
o: To praise students who finish problems quickly and easily
To explain why math is the hardest subject
To show a person who never finds a weak point
To prove that errors are enjoyable
qs.why: 쉬운 문제만 고르면 약점을 발견하지 못한다는 대조 예시예요.

qs.q: What did the teacher NOT mean by her words?
o: Errors can show where understanding ends.
Mistakes are fun to make.
Learning involves some wrong answers.
A wrong answer is a chance to learn.
qs.why: 'She did not mean that mistakes are enjoyable.'

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward mistakes?
o: Angry and critical
Fearful and extremely worried
Bored and uninterested
Positive and encouraging
qs.why: 실수를 정보로 보라는 긍정적이고 격려하는 태도예요.

items.title: The Quiet Power of Bees
items.text: Bees are best known for honey, but their real value lies elsewhere. About one third of the food we eat depends on pollination, the process in which pollen moves from flower to flower so that plants can produce fruit and seeds. Bees carry out much of this work as they travel in search of nectar. In recent years, however, bee numbers have dropped in many regions because of pesticides and the loss of wild flowers. If this trend continues, farmers may have to pollinate crops by hand, which would be slow and extremely expensive. Protecting bees is therefore a way of protecting our own food supply.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Honey is the most valuable thing that bees give us.
Farmers should stop using flowers in their fields.
Bees matter for our food, so they need protection.
Pesticides are too costly for most farmers.
qs.why: 마지막 문장이 요지예요. 벌 보호가 곧 우리 식량 보호예요.

qs.q: According to the passage, why have bee numbers dropped?
o: Because of pesticides and fewer wild flowers
Because honey has become too cheap for beekeepers to sell
Because farmers have started pollinating crops by hand
Because bees prefer to live in cities
qs.why: 'because of pesticides and the loss of wild flowers'

qs.q: In the passage, “pollination” refers to
o: the making of honey inside a crowded hive
the spread of pesticides in the soil
the growing of flowers in a garden
the movement of pollen between flowers
qs.why: 본문에서 pollination을 직접 정의하고 있어요.

qs.q: What would most likely happen if bees continue to disappear?
o: Honey would be sold at lower prices in stores.
Growing some foods would get harder and costlier.
Wild flowers would grow much faster in the fields.
Fewer farmers would need workers on their land.
qs.why: 손으로 수분해야 하고 비용이 많이 든다는 내용에서 추론해요.

items.title: Reading on Paper or on Screen
items.text: Many students now read almost everything on a screen, and the habit is convenient. Still, several studies suggest that people understand long texts better on paper. One explanation is that a printed page has a fixed shape, so readers remember where an idea appeared, such as near the top of the left-hand page. On a scrolling screen, the words move and this mental map is harder to build. Another reason is that screens invite quick skimming. This does not mean that digital reading is useless; it simply means that for a difficult text we should ______.

qs.q: Which phrase best fills the blank?
o: avoid reading long texts on paper or screen altogether
choose a format that supports careful reading
always skim every text quickly to save time at school
read only on screens with bright lights
qs.why: 종이가 깊은 이해에 유리하다는 내용 뒤에 이어질 실용적 결론이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to buy a printed book at a much lower price
Why scrolling is the fastest way to read any text
When students should stop reading books
Why paper may help us understand difficult texts
qs.why: 화면과 종이를 비교하며 종이가 이해에 유리한 이유를 설명해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what tends to happen when people read on screens?
o: They may skim instead of reading closely.
They read more slowly and carefully than on paper.
They understand long texts better than on paper.
They are useless for any kind of reading.
qs.why: 'screens invite quick skimming'이라고 했어요. 화면이 쓸모없다는 뜻은 아니라고 본문이 밝혀요.

qs.q: In the passage, “this mental map” refers to
o: a picture drawn in a school notebook
a route to the school library
a memory of where ideas appeared
a list of difficult words
qs.why: 앞 문장의 remember where an idea appeared를 가리켜요.

items.title: An Unexpected Gift
items.text: Hana had saved for weeks to buy a bicycle, but when she reached the shop, the price had risen. She walked home slowly, trying not to cry. At the door, her neighbor, Mr. Park, was waiting with an old blue bicycle. “My legs are too stiff for riding now,” he said, “and it seems a waste to leave it in the garage.” Hana looked at the scratched frame and the worn seat, and then she smiled. It was not the shiny bicycle she had imagined, but it was better, because someone had thought of her. That evening she rode around the whole neighborhood until the street lights came on.

qs.q: How did Hana feel at the end of the story?
o: Jealous and angry
Embarrassed and nervous
Lonely and bored
Grateful and delighted
qs.why: 자전거를 받고 웃으며 동네를 돌았으므로 고마움과 기쁨이에요.

qs.q: Why did Hana walk home slowly at first?
o: She had lost the money on the way.
The bicycle's price had gone up.
Mr. Park had asked her to wait outside.
The shop was closed for the day.
qs.why: 'the price had risen'

qs.q: Why does the writer say the old bicycle was “better” than a shiny one?
o: It was faster than a new bicycle.
It had been repaired by an expert.
Someone had cared about her feelings.
It was cheaper than any bicycle in the shop.
qs.why: Hana를 생각해 준 사람이 있었기 때문이라고 직접 설명해요.

qs.q: Which of the following is the best theme of the story?
o: Kindness can mean more than a perfect gift.
Saving money for weeks is always a waste of effort.
Old things should always be thrown away.
Neighbors should avoid giving presents.
qs.why: 낡은 자전거지만 마음이 담긴 선물이 더 값지다는 주제예요.

items.title: Sleep and Memory
items.text: Many teenagers believe that staying up all night before a test is a smart strategy. In fact, it often works against them. During sleep, the brain replays what we learned during the day and stores the important parts in long-term memory. When a student skips sleep, this process is cut short, so facts that were studied for hours may disappear quickly. One experiment found that students who slept eight hours after studying recalled far more words than students who stayed awake for the same period. The result suggests that sleep is not time taken away from studying; rather, it is ______.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: a necessary part of learning
an enemy of good grades
a habit only for young children
a choice that has no effect
qs.why: 수면이 기억 저장에 필요하다는 실험 결과에 이어지는 결론이에요.

qs.q: What is the best title of the passage?
o: The Best Way to Study All Night
How to Fall Asleep in Class
Why Sleep Helps You Remember
Eight Hours of Words and Tests
qs.why: 수면이 기억에 도움이 된다는 것이 글의 요지예요.

qs.q: What did the experiment find?
o: Students learned faster at night than in the morning.
Sleepers recalled more words than others.
Eight hours of study led to perfect scores.
Awake students stored facts in long-term memory.
qs.why: 'recalled far more words' 부분이 근거예요.

qs.q: Which of these students is most likely to forget what he studied?
o: A student who reviews his notes and then sleeps well that night
A student who studies for two hours each day
A student who reads a book before going to bed
A student who studies until dawn and does not sleep
qs.why: 수면이 부족하면 기억 저장 과정이 중단돼요.

items.title: A Letter to the Editor
items.text:
To the Editor:

I am writing about the recent decision to shorten the opening hours of our public library. According to the notice, the change will save the city a small amount of money. However, many students depend on the library as a quiet place to study after school, and several older residents use its computers to read the news and keep in touch with relatives. Closing at five o'clock instead of eight will make the library useless to most of these people. I urge the city council to reconsider and to look for savings in other areas.

Sincerely,
Minho Seo

qs.q: Why did the writer write this letter?
o: To announce a new library opening
To thank the city for saving money
To ask the council to change its decision
To advertise computers for older residents
qs.why: 마지막에 council에 재고를 촉구(urge ... reconsider)해요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main argument?
o: Shorter hours would hurt the library's users.
The library should have more computers.
The city should spend less money on newspapers.
Students should study at home after school.
qs.why: 단축 운영이 도서관 이용자에게 피해를 준다는 주장이에요.

qs.q: Who uses the library according to the letter?
o: Teachers and city council members
Newspaper writers and travelers
Children and shop owners
Students and older residents
qs.why: 학생과 노인 주민이 언급돼요.

qs.q: Which word best describes the writer's tone?
o: Joking and careless
Serious and respectful
Sad and completely hopeless
Excited and proud
qs.why: 정중하지만 단호한 어조예요.

items.title: Why Cities Are Getting Hotter
items.text: On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside nearby. Scientists call this the urban heat island effect. Dark roads and roofs absorb the sun's energy and release it slowly at night, while concrete buildings leave little room for trees that would otherwise provide shade and cool the air as water evaporates from their leaves. Because of this, some cities now paint roofs white and plant trees along streets. These measures are simple, but they can lower temperatures noticeably and reduce the need for air conditioning, which itself ______.

qs.q: Which expression best completes the passage?
o: makes buildings darker
adds heat to the outside air
protects the trees from sun
keeps cities colder at night
qs.why: 에어컨은 실외로 열을 내보내 도시를 더 덥게 해요. 앞의 'reduce the need'와 이어져요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The advantages of living in the quiet countryside
The best colors for painting a house
Why air conditioning is cheaper than trees
The causes of city heat and ways to reduce it
qs.why: 원인과 해결책을 소개하는 글이에요.

qs.q: How do trees help cool the air?
o: Water evaporates from their leaves.
They absorb extra heat from the hot roads.
They make roofs turn white.
They release energy at night.
qs.why: 'water evaporates from their leaves'

qs.q: In the passage, “absorb” is closest in meaning to
o: give back
break down
take in
push away
qs.why: absorb는 '흡수하다'예요.

items.title: Two Kinds of Courage
items.text: When we hear the word courage, we usually imagine a firefighter running into a burning building. That kind of bravery is dramatic and easy to admire. There is, however, a quieter form of courage that appears in everyday life: telling the truth when it is uncomfortable, admitting a mistake, or asking for help. These actions rarely win applause, and nobody writes songs about them. Yet they require us to face fear in the same way, because we risk looking weak or being rejected. Perhaps we should learn to value this ordinary courage as much as the heroic kind.

qs.q: What does the writer mainly argue?
o: Firefighters are braver than most other kinds of workers.
Admitting a mistake in public is always a bad idea.
Songs should be written about daily life.
Everyday courage deserves as much respect as heroism.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 일상의 용기도 영웅적 용기만큼 존중하자고 말해요.

qs.q: Which is an example of the “quieter form of courage”?
o: Running into a fire
Asking for help
Winning a prize
Writing a song
qs.why: 본문에서 예로 telling the truth, admitting a mistake, asking for help를 들어요.

qs.q: Why do the quieter acts require courage, according to the writer?
o: They always put people in serious physical danger.
They are performed in front of large crowds.
People may fear looking weak or being rejected.
They are usually rewarded with songs.
qs.why: 'we risk looking weak or being rejected'

qs.q: How does the writer begin the passage?
o: By stating a common view, then adding another
By giving a long list of numbers and facts first
By telling a funny story about a firefighter
By asking readers to vote on a famous hero
qs.why: 흔한 이미지(소방관)를 먼저 보여준 뒤 however로 다른 관점을 제시해요.

items.title: The Price of Free Apps
items.text: Many of the apps on our phones are free, and it is tempting to think that we receive them without paying anything. In fact, the companies that make them earn money in another way. They collect information about what we search for, where we go, and which advertisements we click on, and then they sell advertising space aimed at specific groups. In this system, our attention and personal data are the real product. This does not mean that we should delete every app. It does mean that we should ______ before pressing “Agree.”

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: check what information we are giving away
count how many apps we own and how often we use them
decide which color we prefer
ask when the next update will arrive
qs.why: 개인정보가 상품이라는 앞 내용에 이어 '동의'를 누르기 전 확인해야 할 것이에요.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Phones should be sold without any apps in them.
Advertisements are more useful than apps.
Free apps cost us our personal information.
Companies give apps away to make friends.
qs.why: 무료 앱의 대가는 개인정보라는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: In the passage, “tempting” means
o: too difficult for most users to understand
attractive enough to make us believe it
dangerous for our health
unusual in our time
qs.why: tempting은 '솔깃한, 그렇게 생각하고 싶어지는'이에요.

qs.q: What do app companies sell, according to the passage?
o: New phones and tablets to young people
Maps of the user's neighborhood and school
Free updates for old apps
Advertising space aimed at certain groups
qs.why: 'sell advertising space aimed at specific groups'

items.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
items.text: For thirty years, Mr. Alden lit the lamp of the lighthouse every evening, and his daughter Clara always climbed the stairs beside him. When automatic lights replaced human keepers, the old tower was closed, and Clara thought that everything meaningful had ended. Then the town decided to turn the building into a small museum, and Clara was asked to guide visitors. She told them about storms, ships, and the long nights when her father watched the sea. “The light is no longer needed,” she said at the end of each tour, “but the story of the light is.” The visitors always went away quietly, as if they had seen something precious.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A father decides to leave his small coastal town.
A museum is damaged during a storm.
A woman finds a new purpose for an old place.
Visitors argue about an automatic light.
qs.why: 등대가 박물관이 되고 Clara가 새 역할을 찾는 이야기예요.

qs.q: What does Clara mean by “the story of the light is [needed]”?
o: People still need to remember the past.
Ships will soon return to the old lighthouse.
The lamp must be lit again.
Tourists want to buy new lights.
qs.why: 등대 자체는 쓸모없어도 그 이야기는 기억되어야 한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why was the lighthouse closed?
o: A terrible storm had badly broken the tower.
Clara's father had moved away.
Visitors had stopped coming to it.
Machines began to do the keeper's work.
qs.why: 'automatic lights replaced human keepers'

qs.q: How did Clara feel when the lighthouse was closed?
o: She was relieved to finally leave the lonely tower.
She felt that something important had ended.
She was angry at the museum's guides.
She was excited about meeting visitors.
qs.why: 'thought that everything meaningful had ended'

items.title: Money and Happiness
items.text: It is commonly believed that more money always brings more happiness. Research shows a more complicated picture. When people move out of poverty, their happiness rises sharply because their basic needs, such as food and safety, are finally met. After a certain income, however, extra money produces smaller and smaller improvements. A person who earns twice as much does not feel twice as happy. What matters more, studies suggest, is how money is used: spending it on shared experiences or on helping others tends to bring ______ satisfaction than buying more things for oneself.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: smaller
greater
weaker
fewer
qs.why: 경험과 남을 돕는 데 쓰는 돈이 물건 구매보다 만족이 '더 크다'는 비교 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the best summary of the passage?
o: Wealthy people are always happier than poor people everywhere.
Basic needs have no effect on happiness.
Spending on things guarantees satisfaction.
Money matters up to a point, and its use matters too.
qs.why: 소득 증가의 효과가 줄고, 사용 방식이 중요하다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: What happens when people escape poverty?
o: Their happiness increases quickly.
They feel less safe than before.
Their income stops growing.
They stop sharing with others.
qs.why: 'their happiness rises sharply'

qs.q: Which of the following would the writer most likely agree with?
o: Earning twice as much money makes life twice as good.
Saving money is the only path to joy.
Time with friends may satisfy more than a gadget.
Poverty has little effect on feelings.
qs.why: 경험과 나눔이 물건 구매보다 만족이 크다는 글쓴이의 주장과 일치해요.

items.title: A Notice from the School Garden Club
items.text: Attention, students! The School Garden Club will hold its spring planting day this Saturday from 9 a.m. to noon. We need volunteers to prepare the soil, plant vegetable seeds, and build a small fence around the new beds. No experience is necessary; the club members will show you what to do. Please wear old clothes and bring a water bottle. Everything we grow will be shared with the school cafeteria and with a local food bank. Sign up at the science office by Thursday afternoon, and help us turn an empty corner of the schoolyard into something useful.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the notice?
o: To announce the temporary closing of the school cafeteria
To sell vegetables to the students
To explain how to build a science lab
To ask students to volunteer for a garden project
qs.why: 자원봉사자를 모집하는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: What should the volunteers bring?
o: Their own seeds
A water bottle
A bag of soil
A signed permission note
qs.why: 'bring a water bottle'이라고 했고, 씨앗이나 흙을 가져오라는 말은 없어요.

qs.q: What will happen to the vegetables that grow?
o: They will be sold to raise money for a school trip.
They will be taken home by the volunteers.
They will go to the cafeteria and a food bank.
They will be used only in science class.
qs.why: 'shared with the school cafeteria and with a local food bank'

qs.q: What can be inferred about the volunteers?
o: Beginners are welcome to join.
Only club members can attend.
They must have gardening licenses.
They will work until the evening.
qs.why: 'No experience is necessary'

items.title: What a Map Leaves Out
items.text: Every map is a simplification. A subway map, for example, shows stations in tidy straight lines and equal distances, although the real tunnels bend and stretch unevenly. The mapmaker has deliberately removed these details because passengers do not need them; they only need to know where to change trains. Similarly, a world map must flatten a round planet onto a sheet of paper, and this inevitably changes the size of some countries. These examples show that a map is not a copy of reality but a tool built for a purpose. When we use one, we should therefore ask what it ______ as well as what it shows.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: hides
adds
measures
paints
qs.why: 지도가 무엇을 생략했는지도 물어야 한다는 흐름이에요. 'leaves out'과 같은 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Subway tunnels are always perfectly straight underground.
World maps are the most accurate maps.
Maps serve specific purposes and leave things out.
Passengers prefer maps without stations.
qs.why: 지도는 현실의 복사가 아니라 목적에 맞는 도구라는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: Why does a subway map show equal distances between stations?
o: The tunnels are exactly straight underground.
Passengers mainly need to know where to change.
The mapmaker has no information about the real tunnels.
Equal distances make trains run faster.
qs.why: 'passengers ... only need to know where to change trains'

qs.q: What kind of example does the writer use to support the main idea?
o: A weather forecast and a diary
A recipe and a bus schedule
A photograph and a poem
A subway map and a world map
qs.why: 지하철 노선도와 세계 지도 두 가지를 예로 들어요.

items.title: The Last Day of Exams
items.text: When the bell rang, Jun put down his pencil and let out a long breath. For three weeks he had slept too little, skipped soccer practice, and worried about every subject. Now there was nothing left to study, and the silence in his head felt strange. His friends were already planning a trip to the arcade, but Jun wanted only to walk home alone and listen to the rain. He realized that he was not happy exactly; he was empty, like a glass that had been carried carefully for a long way and was finally set down. Tomorrow, he thought, he would feel like celebrating.

qs.q: Which best describes Jun's feeling at the end of the exams?
o: Proud and excited
Frightened and deeply ashamed
Tired and quietly relieved
Jealous and impatient
qs.why: 축하할 기분이 아니라 비어 있는 듯한 안도감이에요.

qs.q: What does the comparison to “a glass ... set down” suggest?
o: His long effort was over, and he felt drained.
Jun had broken something valuable.
Jun wanted to take a drink of water.
Jun was angry with his friends for leaving him.
qs.why: 조심스럽게 들고 온 잔을 내려놓은 것처럼 긴장이 풀린 상태예요.

qs.q: What did Jun do during the three weeks of exams?
o: He traveled to the arcade.
He slept more than ever.
He walked home in the rain.
He gave up soccer practice.
qs.why: 'skipped soccer practice'

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A plan for a trip to the arcade with friends
A student's feelings after a stressful time
Why exams should last three weeks
A rainy-day soccer game
qs.why: 시험이 끝난 직후의 감정이 중심이에요.

items.title: Do Robots Take Jobs?
items.text: Whenever a new machine appears, people worry that workers will lose their jobs. History gives a mixed answer. When factories began using machines to weave cloth, many weavers did lose their work. But the same machines made cloth cheaper, which increased demand, and new jobs appeared in repairing machines, designing patterns, and selling clothes. Economists expect something similar with modern robots: some tasks will vanish, others will change, and entirely new occupations will appear. The real challenge is not whether work will exist but whether workers can ______ quickly enough to take advantage of it.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: buy more machines
learn new skills
avoid all technology
return to old methods
qs.why: 새로운 직업이 생기므로 변화에 적응할 새 기술 습득이 과제예요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Weavers are the happiest workers in history.
Robots will replace nearly every kind of worker soon.
Clothes were more expensive before factories.
New technology changes work rather than ending it.
qs.why: 기술은 일자리를 없애기도 하지만 바꾸고 새로 만든다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: Why did new jobs appear after machines began to weave cloth?
o: Cheaper cloth increased demand.
Weavers refused to use machines.
Cloth became harder to produce.
Factories closed in many towns.
qs.why: 'made cloth cheaper, which increased demand'

qs.q: How is the passage organized?
o: It lists safety rules for factory workers in cities.
It compares two modern robots.
It uses a past example to talk about the present.
It tells one weaver's life story.
qs.why: 역사적 사례를 들어 현재의 로봇 문제를 논해요.

items.title: Why Stories Matter
items.text: Facts are easy to forget, but stories tend to stay with us. A list of safety rules may be ignored, whereas a short tale about a boy who took a shortcut across thin ice is remembered for years. Scientists explain that stories activate several parts of the brain at once: we imagine the scenes, feel the emotions, and follow the order of events. As a result, information wrapped in a story is easier to recall and more likely to change our behavior. Teachers, doctors, and even business leaders have therefore begun to use stories to ______ important ideas.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: hide
doubt
avoid
teach
qs.why: 이야기가 정보를 더 잘 기억하게 하므로 중요한 생각을 가르치기 위해 쓴다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Safety rules are impossible to write.
Stories help us remember information.
Boys should stay away from thin ice.
Brains work better with fewer emotions.
qs.why: 이야기가 기억과 행동 변화에 효과적이라는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a way stories affect the brain?
o: We imagine the scenes in detail.
We feel the emotions.
They reduce the need for sleep.
We follow the order of events.
qs.why: 수면 감소는 언급되지 않아요.

qs.q: In the passage, “whereas” introduces
o: a contrast between rules and tales
a reason for forgetting facts so easily
an example of a safe shortcut
a result of reading too fast
qs.why: whereas는 '반면에'라는 대조 표현이에요.

items.title: Weekend Market
items.text: Every Saturday morning, the square near my grandmother's house changes into a market. Farmers arrive before dawn with baskets of peaches, bundles of green onions, and large rounds of cheese. By eight o'clock the air smells of fresh bread, and the sellers are calling out the day's prices in cheerful voices. My grandmother knows nearly everyone by name; she says the tomatoes taste better when you know the person who grew them. I used to find the crowds tiring, but now I enjoy listening to the chatter and watching strangers become friends over a few coins and a bag of fruit.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The lively atmosphere of a neighborhood market
How to grow tomatoes in a small home garden
The history of the old town square and its fountain
Why markets are cheaper than stores
qs.why: 시장의 활기찬 분위기를 묘사한 글이에요.

qs.q: What does the grandmother's remark about the tomatoes suggest?
o: Tomatoes grow better in the soil near the square.
Strangers sell the best fruit.
Personal relationships make food more enjoyable.
Prices matter more than flavor.
qs.why: 아는 사람이 키웠기에 더 맛있다는 말은 관계가 즐거움을 더한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How has the writer's feeling about the market changed?
o: From fond of the market to afraid of it
From tired of crowds to fond of them
From proud of the farmers to angry at them
From curious about prices to bored by them
qs.why: 'used to find the crowds tiring, but now I enjoy'

qs.q: What time do the farmers arrive?
o: At eight o'clock
At noon
In the evening
Before dawn
qs.why: 'arrive before dawn'

items.title: Boredom and Creativity
items.text: Modern life offers almost no empty moments. Whenever we wait for a bus or stand in a line, we reach for our phones. Psychologists warn that this habit may carry a hidden cost. When the mind has nothing to do, it begins to wander, connecting memories and ideas that would normally stay apart. In one study, people who first performed a dull task, such as copying phone numbers, afterward came up with more original uses for a plastic cup than people who had not been bored. The finding suggests that occasional boredom is not a waste of time but a kind of ______ for the imagination.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: injury
noise
training
prize
qs.why: 지루함이 창의성에 도움이 된다는 실험 결과의 결론이에요.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Boredom can help the mind create new ideas.
Waiting in line is the best use of time.
Phones should be banned from every bus.
Copying numbers is a fun hobby for scientists.
qs.why: 지루함이 창의성을 키운다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: What did people do before thinking of uses for a plastic cup?
o: They talked with strangers.
They played a phone game.
They drew pictures of cups.
They did a dull task.
qs.why: 'performed a dull task, such as copying phone numbers'

qs.q: Why does the writer mention phones in the first part?
o: To advertise a new product to young readers
To show how people avoid empty moments
To prove phones are expensive
To explain how to copy numbers
qs.why: 빈 시간을 피하려는 습관의 예로 휴대폰을 들어요.

items.title: Plastic in the Ocean
items.text: Each year, millions of tons of plastic waste flow into the sea. Large pieces harm animals directly: turtles mistake bags for jellyfish, and seabirds become tangled in old fishing lines. Over time, however, sunlight and waves break the plastic into tiny fragments that can be eaten by even the smallest creatures. These fragments enter the food chain and may eventually reach the fish that people eat. Cleaning beaches is helpful, but experts say it is not enough. The most effective solution is to ______ the amount of plastic that enters the water in the first place.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: increase
reduce
ignore
measure only
qs.why: 문제의 근원을 줄이는 것이 가장 효과적이라는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Jellyfish are the main food of all sea turtles and birds.
Beaches are cleaner now than they used to be before.
Seabirds prefer eating plastic to old fishing lines.
Plastic harms sea life and must be cut at the source.
qs.why: 피해를 설명하고 근본적 감소를 주장해요.

qs.q: How do large pieces of plastic hurt animals?
o: Animals eat them or get caught in them.
They make the water too warm for fish to live.
They block sunlight for all fish.
They are used as nests by seabirds.
qs.why: bags를 해파리로 착각하고 낚싯줄에 얽힌다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about tiny plastic fragments?
o: They disappear quickly when the sunlight is strong.
They are harmless to small creatures.
They can eventually be a problem for human food.
They stay only on beaches.
qs.why: 먹이 사슬을 거쳐 사람이 먹는 물고기에 도달할 수 있어요.

items.title: An Email to a Teammate
items.text:
Subject: About Friday's presentation

Hi Dana,

Thank you for sending the slides so quickly. I read them last night, and I think the opening is strong. My only concern is the third section, which has too many numbers on one page. If the audience tries to read everything, they may stop listening to us. Could we keep only the three most important figures and move the rest to an appendix? I can rewrite the section tomorrow morning if you agree. Let me know what you think before our meeting at four.

Best,
Eli

qs.q: Why did Eli write this email?
o: To cancel the presentation planned for Friday
To complain about a late delivery
To introduce himself to a new teammate
To suggest a change to part of the slides
qs.why: 3번 섹션의 숫자를 줄이자는 제안이 목적이에요.

qs.q: What does Eli think about the opening of the presentation?
o: It is too long.
It is strong.
It needs new slides.
It has too many numbers.
qs.why: 'I think the opening is strong.'

qs.q: Why does Eli worry about the numbers?
o: The numbers may be wrong in some slides.
The meeting may end too late.
The audience may stop listening.
The slides may not open.
qs.why: 'they may stop listening to us'

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone of the email?
o: Polite and cooperative
Angry and extremely demanding
Nervous and confused
Cold and distant
qs.why: 고마움을 표하고 부드럽게 제안하는 협조적인 어조예요.

items.title: Learning a Language as an Adult
items.text: Many adults give up on a new language because they believe children learn faster. Children do pick up accents more easily, but adults have advantages of their own. They already understand how grammar works, they can use study strategies, and they can link new words to a wide range of experiences. Research even shows that adult beginners often make quicker progress in the first months. What matters most over time is not age but consistency: twenty minutes of practice every day is far more effective than a single long session once a week, because memory is strengthened by ______.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: regular repetition
long periods of silence
sudden pressure
occasional luck
qs.why: 매일 조금씩 연습이 낫다는 근거는 반복이 기억을 강화한다는 것이에요.

qs.q: What is the best title of the passage?
o: Why Children Never Learn Grammar
The Danger of Very Long Study Sessions
Adults Can Learn Languages Well Too
Accents Are the Key to Success
qs.why: 성인 학습자의 장점과 꾸준함을 강조하는 글이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what do children do more easily than adults?
o: Understand grammar
Pick up accents
Use study strategies
Link words to experiences
qs.why: 'Children do pick up accents more easily'

qs.q: Which learner will probably make the most progress?
o: One who studies only on Sunday for many hours
One who waits for a perfect accent first
One who avoids grammar rules
One who studies for a short time every day
qs.why: 꾸준한 짧은 연습이 가장 효과적이에요.

items.title: The Marathon Runner
items.text: Mina had never run more than five kilometers when she signed up for the city marathon. Friends told her she was being unrealistic, but she trained every morning, increasing her distance a little each week. On race day, her legs ached after thirty kilometers, and for a moment she wanted to stop. Then she remembered the early mornings, the cold rain, and the promise she had made to herself. She slowed down, drank some water, and kept going. When she crossed the finish line, her time was not impressive, but she was crying with joy. “I did not beat the others,” she said later. “I beat the girl who thought she could not.”

qs.q: What is the main message of the story?
o: Training every morning in the rain is always dangerous.
Friends are usually right about difficult plans like races.
Overcoming your doubts can matter more than winning.
A fast time is the only proof of success.
qs.why: 마지막 말이 핵심이에요. 다른 사람이 아니라 스스로의 의심을 이겼다는 것이에요.

qs.q: How did Mina feel when she finished?
o: Happy and moved
Disappointed and ashamed
Bored and sleepy
Angry and confused
qs.why: 기쁨에 눈물을 흘렸어요.

qs.q: What does “the girl who thought she could not” refer to?
o: One of her friends
Another runner in the race
A girl from a news story
Mina's earlier self
qs.why: 자신의 과거 자신을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What did Mina do when her legs ached?
o: She asked a friend to run with her.
She slowed down and drank water.
She left the race at once.
She ran faster to finish early.
qs.why: 'She slowed down, drank some water, and kept going.'

items.title: What Makes a Good Neighbor
items.text: In a large apartment building, it is possible to live for years without learning the names of the people next door. Yet when a sudden problem occurs, such as a power cut or a lost key, a friendly neighbor can be more useful than any service. Good neighbors do not need to become close friends. They simply greet one another, keep the noise down at night, and notice when something seems wrong. These small habits build trust, and trust makes a community safer. Therefore, the first step toward a better neighborhood is not a new rule but a simple ______.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: fence
hello
complaint
contract
qs.why: 작은 인사 습관이 신뢰를 만든다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Apartment buildings are always noisy.
Neighbors must become close friends.
Services can replace friends during emergencies.
Small friendly habits make a neighborhood safer.
qs.why: 사소한 친절한 습관이 공동체를 안전하게 만든다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a habit of a good neighbor?
o: Lending money regularly
Greeting others
Keeping noise down at night
Noticing when something is wrong
qs.why: 돈을 빌려주는 것은 언급되지 않아요.

qs.q: In the passage, “trust” means
o: a feeling of boredom
a large amount of money in a bank
belief that others are reliable
a rule written on paper
qs.why: trust는 '신뢰'예요.

items.title: A Museum Review
items.text: The new Museum of Everyday Objects does not contain gold crowns or famous paintings. Instead, it displays things we normally ignore: a worn-out spoon, a pair of glasses, a handwritten shopping list. Each item is shown with a short story from the person who used it, and the effect is surprisingly moving. Standing in front of a chipped teacup, I found myself thinking of my own grandfather's morning routine. The building itself is small, and the lighting is occasionally too dim to read the labels. Even so, I would recommend the museum to anyone who wants to see how ordinary lives become history.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To warn people about a closed museum
To describe a famous painting
To collect old spoons
To recommend a museum to readers
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 박물관을 추천해요.

qs.q: What is one weakness of the museum mentioned in the review?
o: The tickets are too expensive for most families.
The lighting is sometimes too dim.
The building is extremely large.
The stories are too long.
qs.why: 'the lighting is occasionally too dim'

qs.q: Why did the teacup make the writer think of his or her grandfather?
o: It was exactly the same cup as his own.
It was shown beside a famous painting by a master.
It reminded the writer of a daily habit.
It was made of gold.
qs.why: 할아버지의 아침 일과가 떠올랐다고 해요.

qs.q: In the passage, “moving” is closest in meaning to
o: emotionally touching
quickly changing in size
physically heavy
difficult to read
qs.why: 여기서 moving은 '감동적인'이에요.

items.title: The Problem with Perfect
items.text: Perfectionists often believe that high standards are the key to success. Unfortunately, the opposite can happen. Because they fear making any error, they delay starting a task until conditions seem perfect, and when they finally begin, they spend too long on small details. Some even avoid challenges entirely rather than risk failing. Psychologists suggest a different goal: aim for “good enough” on the first attempt and improve it later. A rough draft that exists is more valuable than a flawless one that ______.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: is never written
is shared with friends
takes only an hour
has a clear title
qs.why: 시작하지 못하는 완벽주의의 문제를 대비시키는 문장이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to write the most flawless first draft ever
Why challenges should always be avoided
Why aiming for perfection can prevent progress
What psychologists do in their offices
qs.why: 완벽주의가 오히려 진행을 막는다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: What do perfectionists often do?
o: They finish every task much earlier than others.
They delay starting until things feel perfect.
They ignore small details.
They accept rough drafts happily.
qs.why: 'delay starting a task until conditions seem perfect'

qs.q: What would the writer probably advise a student with a difficult essay?
o: Wait until all of the ideas are completely perfect.
Choose an easier topic.
Ask a teacher to write it.
Start with a rough draft and revise it later.
qs.why: 'good enough' 초안을 먼저 쓰라는 조언이에요.

items.title: Volcanoes: Destroyers and Creators
items.text: When a volcano erupts, the news usually shows burning rivers of lava and clouds of ash. These images are frightening, and the damage can be severe. Yet volcanoes also create. Many islands, such as those in the Pacific Ocean, were built layer by layer from cooled lava. Volcanic ash, though harmful when it falls, breaks down over time and enriches the soil with minerals, which is why farmers have long grown crops on the slopes of ancient volcanoes. In short, the same force that threatens life can later ______ it.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: end
forget
support
weaken
qs.why: 파괴적인 힘이 나중에 생명을 돕는다는 대조예요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Volcanoes destroy but also create land and soil.
Lava is the only danger that a volcano brings to people.
Farmers should stay away from all mountains and hills.
Pacific islands are slowly built by sea animals alone.
qs.why: 파괴와 창조의 양면을 설명해요.

qs.q: Why do farmers grow crops near old volcanoes?
o: The lava keeps the plants warm in winter.
The ash protects fields from rain.
The slopes are flat and wide.
The soil is enriched with minerals.
qs.why: 'enriches the soil with minerals'

qs.q: Which word signals a change in the writer's view?
o: When
Yet
Many
Over
qs.why: Yet 이후에 volcanoes also create로 관점이 전환돼요.

items.title: Why Teenagers Need Time Alone
items.text: Parents often worry when a teenager spends hours alone in a bedroom. Psychologists, however, point out that solitude can be healthy. In private, young people sort out their feelings, think about who they are, and recover from the constant demands of social life. The key difference is between being alone by choice and being left out against one's will. The first brings calm and self-knowledge; the second brings pain. Parents therefore need to ______ whether the quiet is a chosen rest or a sign of loneliness before deciding to step in.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: punish
notice
pretend
forbid
qs.why: 선택한 혼자 있음인지 외로움인지를 알아차려야 한다는 흐름이에요. 'notice whether'가 자연스러워요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Teenagers should never be allowed in their bedrooms.
Parents must keep children busy at all times.
Social life is more harmful than loneliness.
Spending time alone can be good if it is chosen.
qs.why: 선택한 혼자만의 시간은 건강할 수 있다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what does chosen solitude bring?
o: Calm and self-knowledge
Pain and anger
Noise and constant demands
Popularity and fame
qs.why: 'The first brings calm and self-knowledge'

qs.q: Which situation would worry the writer?
o: A teenager who reads comics alone in his room for fun
A teenager who draws quietly after school
A teenager left out by friends against his will
A teenager who rests after a busy week
qs.why: 원치 않게 소외된 외로움이 걱정스러운 경우예요.

items.title: The Bike-Sharing Experiment
items.text: When the city of Lakeside introduced bike-sharing stations, officials expected tourists to be the main users. To their surprise, the largest group turned out to be office workers who rode for short trips between meetings. Bicycles were faster than buses in the crowded center, and there was no need to look for a parking space. As the number of riders grew, the city added bike lanes, which in turn encouraged even more people to ride. Officials now describe the program as a success, though they admit that rainy weather and broken bikes remain serious problems.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why tourists dislike riding in the rain
How to repair broken bicycles
The history of parking spaces
A bike program with unexpected results
qs.why: 예상과 다른 이용자층에서 성공한 자전거 공유 프로그램이에요.

qs.q: Who used the bikes the most?
o: Tourists
Office workers
Students
Delivery drivers
qs.why: 'the largest group turned out to be office workers'

qs.q: What can be inferred from “which in turn encouraged even more people”?
o: Bike lanes made the bikes more expensive to rent.
Fewer people wanted to ride.
Lanes and riders helped each other grow.
Buses stopped running in the center.
qs.why: 자전거 도로가 이용자를 늘리고 이용자가 늘어 도로가 더 생기는 순환이에요.

qs.q: How do city officials feel about the program?
o: Pleased but aware of remaining problems
Disappointed and ready to stop the program
Angry at office workers
Uninterested in the results
qs.why: 성공이라고 하면서도 문제점을 인정해요.

items.title: A Summer Camp Advertisement
items.text: Discover the outdoors at Pine Ridge Adventure Camp! For two weeks in July, young people aged 12 to 16 can try kayaking, rock climbing, and wilderness cooking under the guidance of trained instructors. Our small groups of ten ensure that everyone receives personal attention. In the evenings, campers share stories around the fire and learn teamwork through friendly challenges. No previous experience is necessary, and all equipment is provided. Places are limited, so register before June 1 to guarantee your spot. Come for the activities, and leave with new friends and new confidence.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this advertisement?
o: To encourage young people to join a camp
To report an accident at a lake
To teach cooking skills to young people
To announce a new school rule for campers
qs.why: 캠프 참가를 권유하는 광고예요.

qs.q: What does a camper need to bring for the activities, according to the ad?
o: His or her own kayak
A letter from a teacher
No special equipment
Rock-climbing shoes
qs.why: 'all equipment is provided'이므로 따로 장비를 가져올 필요가 없어요.

qs.q: Until when should people register?
o: July 1
June 1
The first day of camp
Any day in July
qs.why: 'register before June 1'

qs.q: Which of the following is suggested by the advertisement?
o: Campers will practice working as a team.
Only experts will be accepted.
The camp lasts all summer.
Groups are very large.
qs.why: 'learn teamwork through friendly challenges'와 작은 모둠 활동에서 팀워크를 연습한다고 추론할 수 있어요.

items.title: When Silence Speaks
items.text: In some cultures, silence in a conversation is a sign of respect. The listener waits, thinks, and replies only when the thought is complete. In other cultures, a pause of just a few seconds can feel uncomfortable, and people hurry to fill it. Misunderstandings occur when these habits meet. A person who values quick answers may think a silent partner is uninterested, while the silent partner may think the fast talker is rude for interrupting thoughts. Recognizing that both styles are valid can help us ______ rather than judge.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: interrupt
complain
listen
compete
qs.why: 두 방식이 모두 타당함을 알면 판단하기보다 귀 기울이게 돼요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Silence is useless and should be avoided in every conversation.
Fast talkers are always rude people who ruin conversations.
All cultures value quick answers more than careful thought.
Different attitudes toward silence can cause misunderstandings.
qs.why: 침묵에 대한 문화적 차이가 오해를 낳는다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: How do some cultures regard silence?
o: As a sign of great anger
As a waste of time
As a rude habit
As a sign of respect
qs.why: 'silence ... is a sign of respect'

qs.q: What would a quick talker probably think of a silent partner?
o: The partner is very polite.
The partner is not interested.
The partner is speaking too fast.
The partner is angry about the weather.
qs.why: 빠른 대답을 중시하는 사람은 침묵을 무관심으로 오해할 수 있어요.

items.title: The Orchestra Without a Leader
items.text: Most orchestras are led by a conductor who decides the speed and style of the music. Yet a few groups perform without one. In these orchestras, the musicians watch and listen to each other closely, and leadership passes from one player to another depending on the piece. Rehearsals take longer because every decision must be discussed, and disagreements are common. Still, the members say the result is a performance in which everyone feels responsible. Such an example reminds us that a group can work well without a single boss as long as its members ______.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: avoid all discussion among themselves
listen carefully to one another
play different pieces
practice alone at home
qs.why: 서로를 주의 깊게 보고 듣는 것이 지휘자 없이 연주하는 비결이에요.

qs.q: What does the passage mainly show?
o: Conductors are not needed in any kind of orchestra.
Rehearsals should always be short.
Disagreement is a sign of failure.
A group can succeed by sharing responsibility.
qs.why: 단일 지도자 없이도 책임을 나누면 잘 돌아간다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: Why do rehearsals take longer in orchestras without a conductor?
o: Every decision has to be discussed.
The musicians arrive late.
The pieces are very short.
The instruments are harder to play.
qs.why: 'every decision must be discussed'

qs.q: In the passage, “responsible” is closest in meaning to
o: unable to play any music at all
unwilling to listen to others
in charge of part of the result
free from every duty and care
qs.why: responsible은 '책임이 있는'이에요.

items.title: A Fisherman's Lesson
items.text: An old fisherman sat every day on the same rock, casting his line into the calm bay. A young tourist watched him for a week and finally said, “You could catch far more fish with a boat and a net, and then you could buy more boats and hire people.” The fisherman smiled. “And then?” “Then you could retire and fish on a rock in a quiet bay.” The old man laughed softly. “That is what I am doing now.” The tourist opened his mouth to speak, but no words came. He realized that he had been rushing toward something the old man already had.

qs.q: What is the lesson of the story?
o: Boats and nets always make fishing much easier.
Tourists should never talk to strangers.
Quiet bays are the best place for business.
We may already have what we are looking for.
qs.why: 목표를 위해 달리는 사람에게 이미 가진 것의 가치를 일깨워요.

qs.q: Why did the tourist fail to answer?
o: He was angry about the fisherman's laugh.
He saw that his advice made little sense.
He did not understand the fisherman's language.
He wanted to buy the fisherman's boat.
qs.why: 자신이 좇는 목표를 노인이 이미 이루고 있다는 점을 깨달았어요.

qs.q: How long did the tourist watch the fisherman before speaking?
o: A day
A month
A week
An hour
qs.why: 'watched him for a week'

qs.q: How would you describe the fisherman's manner?
o: Calm and content
Proud and greedy
Worried and shy
Rude and impatient
qs.why: 차분하게 웃고 만족해 있어요.

items.title: The Rise of Online Learning
items.text: Online courses have changed the way people study. A student in a small village can now watch a lecture from a famous university without traveling anywhere, and a worker can learn a new skill late at night. Convenience, however, brings its own difficulties. Without a teacher in the room, many learners lose motivation, and a large number never finish the courses they begin. Successful online students tend to set a regular schedule, join discussion groups, and tell friends about their goals. In other words, technology provides the opportunity, but ______ still has to provide the effort.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: the learner
the lecture
the university
the village
qs.why: 기회는 기술이, 노력은 학습자가 제공해야 한다는 대비예요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Online courses offer convenience but also real difficulties.
Universities should close all of their classrooms soon.
Evening is always the best time for watching lectures.
Teachers are no longer needed in any school at all.
qs.why: 온라인 강의의 편리함과 어려움, 그리고 성공하는 학습자의 습관을 다루는 글이에요.

qs.q: What do successful online students tend to do?
o: They watch lectures only once.
They set regular schedules.
They avoid discussion groups.
They keep their goals secret.
qs.why: 'set a regular schedule, join discussion groups, and tell friends'

qs.q: Which word in the passage signals a contrast between the benefits and the difficulties of online study?
o: late
famous
however
regular
qs.why: Convenience, however, brings its own difficulties에서 however가 장점에서 어려움으로 넘어가는 전환을 나타내요.

items.title: Why Honey Never Spoils
items.text: Archaeologists have opened ancient tombs and found jars of honey that were still safe to eat after thousands of years. The secret lies in honey's chemistry. It contains very little water, and the few microbes that land in it cannot survive because the sugar draws moisture out of their cells. In addition, bees add a substance that produces a small amount of a germ-killing chemical. Because spoiling requires living organisms to grow, honey simply gives them no chance. The same principle explains why people have long preserved fruit in sugar: what stops decay is not the age of the food but its ______.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: appearance
packaging
chemistry
texture
qs.why: 썩지 않는 이유는 꿀의 화학적 성질(많은 당분, 적은 수분) 때문이라는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why honey can last so long without going bad
How archaeologists find old jars in ancient tombs
Why bees are important to farmers
How fruit is grown in sugar
qs.why: 꿀이 썩지 않는 이유가 중심이에요.

qs.q: Why can microbes not survive in honey?
o: The honey is always kept very cold in the jars.
The jars have no air.
Bees remove them by hand.
The sugar pulls water out of their cells.
qs.why: 'the sugar draws moisture out of their cells'

qs.q: What can be inferred from the passage about preserved fruit?
o: Fruit never contains water.
Sugar creates conditions that stop decay.
Honey is added to every kind of fruit as well.
Fruit lasts longer if it is old.
qs.why: 꿀과 같은 원리로 설탕이 부패를 막아요.

items.title: Choosing a Club
items.text:
Mia: Have you decided which club to join this semester?
Tom: Not yet. The debate club sounds exciting, but I'm afraid I'll get nervous speaking in front of people.
Mia: That's exactly why you should join. Nobody becomes confident by avoiding what scares them.
Tom: True, but I also have the science exams next month, and the debate club meets twice a week.
Mia: Hmm. Maybe start with the photography club? It only meets on Fridays.
Tom: That's tempting, but I don't even own a camera.
Mia: Most members use their phones. Besides, you might discover a hobby you didn't know you had.
Tom: You make a good point. I'll visit the Friday meeting and then decide about debate next term.

qs.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
o: Planning a science experiment
Deciding which school club to join
Buying a new camera for a school club
Preparing for a speech contest
qs.why: 동아리 선택에 대한 대화예요.

qs.q: Why is Tom hesitant about the debate club?
o: He dislikes photography and the Friday meetings.
He has no time on Fridays.
He wants to leave the school.
He fears public speaking and has exams soon.
qs.why: 발표가 걱정되고 시험이 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What does Mia imply when she says, “Nobody becomes confident by avoiding what scares them”?
o: Facing a fear is how confidence grows.
Debate is the easiest club to join.
Confident people never feel scared at all.
Tom should stay away from clubs.
qs.why: 두려움을 피하면 자신감이 생기지 않는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Tom most likely do next?
o: Join the debate club immediately this week
Buy an expensive camera
Attend a photography meeting on Friday
Give up all clubs this year
qs.why: 마지막에 금요일 모임에 가 보겠다고 해요.

items.title: The Phone Rule
items.text:
Ms. Lee: Class, the school board wants to ban phones during the whole school day. I'd like to hear your opinions.
Jiho: I think it's too strict. We use our phones for dictionaries and for checking schedules.
Ms. Lee: A fair point. Sora, what do you think?
Sora: Honestly, I agree with the ban. When phones are allowed, half the class is checking messages instead of listening.
Jiho: But a total ban doesn't teach responsibility. We should learn to control ourselves.
Sora: That sounds nice, but many of us can't. I know I can't.
Ms. Lee: Perhaps there is a middle path: phones stay in bags except when a teacher allows them for learning.
Jiho: I could accept that.
Sora: Me too, as long as the rule is the same for everyone.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: A plan to buy school dictionaries for all students
A complaint about a teacher's schedule
A new homework policy for math
A debate over how to handle phones at school
qs.why: 학교에서의 휴대폰 사용 규정에 대한 토론이에요.

qs.q: What is Jiho's argument against the total ban?
o: It makes paper dictionaries much more expensive.
It does not teach students responsibility.
It lets teachers use phones freely.
It gives students too much homework.
qs.why: 'a total ban doesn't teach responsibility'

qs.q: Why does Sora support the ban?
o: She never uses a phone.
She wants longer lunch breaks.
She knows messages easily distract her.
She dislikes using dictionaries at school.
qs.why: 스스로를 통제하지 못함을 인정해요.

qs.q: How does the conversation end?
o: The speakers agree on a compromise.
Ms. Lee cancels the discussion early.
Sora refuses any new rule.
Jiho leaves the classroom angrily.
qs.why: 휴대폰은 가방에 두고 필요할 때만 쓰는 절충안에 동의해요.

items.title: A Job Interview Tip
items.text:
Dad: You look worried. Is it about tomorrow's interview at the bakery?
Eun: Yes. I keep thinking they'll ask me something I can't answer.
Dad: What if they ask why you want the job?
Eun: I'd say I like baking, but that sounds too ordinary.
Dad: Ordinary isn't bad if it's true. Add a short story, such as the first cake you made for your grandmother.
Eun: That's a nice idea. It shows who I am, not just what I like.
Dad: Exactly. Interviewers remember stories more than slogans. And don't forget to ask them a question at the end.
Eun: Like what?
Dad: Something simple, such as what a typical morning is like. It shows you are interested.

qs.q: What is the dad mainly doing in the conversation?
o: Advising Eun how to prepare for an interview
Asking Eun to quit her job
Teaching Eun to bake a cake for the interview
Complaining about a bakery
qs.why: 면접 준비 조언이에요.

qs.q: What does Eun worry about?
o: Arriving late at the bakery tomorrow morning
Forgetting her grandmother's recipe
Being asked a question she cannot answer
Having too many interviewers
qs.why: 'they'll ask me something I can't answer'

qs.q: Why does Dad suggest telling a short story?
o: Stories are required by the bakery's rules.
A story makes her answer personal and memorable.
Slogans are impossible to learn.
The interviewers enjoy listening to long speeches.
qs.why: 이야기가 더 기억에 남고 자신을 보여준다는 이유예요.

qs.q: What does Dad recommend doing at the end of the interview?
o: Thanking everyone with a gift
Leaving quietly
Offering to bake a cake
Asking a simple question
qs.why: 'ask them a question at the end'

items.title: Planning a Trip on a Budget
items.text:
Lena: I've found a hotel by the beach for our trip, but it costs twice what we planned.
Sam: That's way over our budget. Is there anything cheaper?
Lena: A hostel in the old town. It's farther from the sea, but the reviews are good.
Sam: How far is it?
Lena: About twenty minutes by bus.
Sam: That's not bad. We could save enough to pay for a boat tour.
Lena: But I wanted to wake up and see the waves from the window.
Sam: I understand. How about staying at the hotel for one night, just as a treat, and the hostel for the rest?
Lena: Now that's a compromise I can live with.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: Booking a boat tour for tomorrow morning
Choosing a bus route
Finding a place to stay within a budget
Writing hotel reviews for a travel site
qs.why: 예산에 맞는 숙소 정하기가 중심이에요.

qs.q: Why does Lena prefer the beach hotel?
o: She wants to see the waves from her window.
It is much cheaper than the old-town hostel.
It has a boat tour.
It is closer to the old town than the hostel.
qs.why: 'I wanted to wake up and see the waves'

qs.q: What do they finally decide?
o: To cancel the trip
To book only the hotel
To walk to the old town
To stay at both places
qs.why: 하룻밤은 호텔, 나머지는 호스텔로 해요.

qs.q: How does Lena feel about Sam's last suggestion?
o: Annoyed
Satisfied
Bored
Surprised by the cost
qs.why: 'a compromise I can live with'는 만족한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Science Project
items.text:
Haru: Our experiment didn't work. The plants in the dark box grew taller than the ones in the sun.
Ms. Cho: That's interesting. Why do you think that happened?
Haru: I don't know. I expected the sunny ones to do better.
Ms. Cho: Look at the data again. What else do you notice about the dark ones?
Haru: They're taller but very pale and thin.
Ms. Cho: Exactly. Plants without light stretch upward searching for it, but they can't make healthy leaves. So your experiment worked after all.
Haru: Because we learned something we didn't expect?
Ms. Cho: Yes. Unexpected results often teach more than the expected ones. Write that in your report.

qs.q: What is the main point Ms. Cho makes?
o: Plants always grow better in the dark than in light.
Surprising results can still be valuable.
Experiments should be repeated three times.
Reports should be short.
qs.why: 예상 밖 결과가 더 많이 가르칠 수 있다는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: How did the plants in the dark box look?
o: Short, green, and strong
Tall and healthy
Dead and dry
Tall but pale and thin
qs.why: 'taller but very pale and thin'

qs.q: Why did the dark-box plants grow so tall?
o: They were stretching to find light.
They received far too much water.
They were kept in a much warmer room.
They had more space for leaves.
qs.why: 빛을 찾아 위로 뻗은 것이에요.

qs.q: How does Haru feel at the beginning of the conversation?
o: Overjoyed
Amused
Let down
Delighted
qs.why: 'Our experiment didn't work'에서 실망감이 드러나요.

items.title: Feedback on an Essay
items.text:
Seo: Mr. Han, thank you for reading my essay. Was it good?
Mr. Han: You have strong ideas, Seo. The problem is the order. Your best argument appears at the very end.
Seo: I wanted to build up to it.
Mr. Han: That works in a story, but in an essay the reader needs your main point early. Otherwise, they read the first three paragraphs without knowing where you are going.
Seo: So I should move the best argument to the beginning?
Mr. Han: Put it in your first paragraph, then use the rest to support it.
Seo: I see. And the conclusion?
Mr. Han: Remind the reader of your point in new words, instead of adding fresh ideas at the last moment.

qs.q: What does Mr. Han mainly give Seo?
o: A grade for the final exam in English
A list of new essay topics for next term
A warning about late homework in class
Advice on how to organize an essay
qs.why: 에세이 구성에 관한 조언이에요.

qs.q: What is the problem with Seo's essay?
o: The ideas are weak.
The best argument comes too late.
The paragraphs are all far too short.
The spelling is full of errors.
qs.why: 'Your best argument appears at the very end.'

qs.q: Why did Seo put the best argument last?
o: He forgot to include it earlier.
He wanted a longer essay.
He wanted to build up to it.
He misread the topic.
qs.why: Seo가 직접 'I wanted to build up to it'라고 말해요.

qs.q: What should the conclusion do, according to Mr. Han?
o: Restate the main point in different words
Add several brand new ideas at the end
Repeat the first paragraph exactly
Ask the reader a very long question at the end
qs.why: 'Remind the reader of your point in new words'

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

The new restaurant looked wonderful in photographs, but the food was bland and the service slow. The meal was a real ______ after all the praise we had read online.
o: letdown
celebration
discovery
bargain
items.why: 기대와 달리 음식이 별로였으므로 disappointment(실망)가 맞아요.

items.q:
Read the paragraph and choose its main idea.

Long before alarm clocks existed, people woke with the sun. Today, artificial light lets us stay awake late into the night, and our bodies often struggle to keep a natural rhythm. Scientists say that exposure to morning daylight helps reset this internal clock.
o: Alarm clocks were invented by farmers long ago.
People should never use lights after sunset.
Morning light can help reset the body's clock.
Sleeping late is a sign of strong health.
items.why: 마지막 문장이 요지예요. 아침 햇빛이 생체 시계를 맞춰요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

A good leader does not simply give orders. She listens to her team, asks questions, and ______ before making a decision, so that everyone feels the final choice is fair.
o: ignores any advice from others
considers different opinions
keeps every idea secret
waits for others to fail
items.why: 듣고 질문한다는 앞 내용에 이어지는 말이에요.

items.q:
Which sentence is NOT needed in the paragraph?

(1) Moving to a new school can be stressful. (2) Students must make new friends and learn unfamiliar rules. (3) Many schools offer sports clubs after class. (4) A friendly welcome from classmates can make the change much easier.
items.why: (3)은 전학의 스트레스와 환영이라는 흐름과 관계가 없어요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

The scientist's theory seemed strange at first, but after years of experiments proved it correct, even her harshest critics were forced to ______ that she had been right.
o: deny
forget
admit
hide
items.why: 실험이 증명했으므로 비판자들도 인정할 수밖에 없다는 흐름이에요.

items.q:
Choose the sentence that best summarizes the paragraph.

Some people enjoy cooking because it is a way to relax. Others cook because they want to save money or eat healthier food. Whatever the reason, learning to prepare a simple meal gives a person independence.
o: Learning to cook has several benefits.
Restaurants are too expensive for most people.
Relaxing is the only good reason to cook.
Healthy food is always difficult to prepare.
items.why: 여러 이유가 있지만 요리를 배우면 이점이 있다는 내용이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

Because the village had no bridge, children had to cross a fast river each morning to reach school. The new bridge has made their daily trip not only quicker but also ______.
o: more expensive
less useful
far noisier
much safer
items.why: 다리가 생겨 빨라졌을 뿐 아니라 안전해졌다는 흐름이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best title for the passage.

Every spring, thousands of birds stop at the wetland near our town. They rest and feed there before continuing their long journey north. Without this safe place, many of them would not have the strength to reach their destination.
o: How to Build a Safe House for Wild Birds
A Resting Place for Travelers of the Sky
The Fastest Birds in the Whole World Today
Why Spring Comes Early in Town
items.why: 철새가 쉬어 가는 습지에 관한 글이므로 이 제목이 가장 알맞아요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

At first, the manager refused to change the schedule. When the workers explained how tired they were, however, he began to ______ and finally agreed to give them an extra day off.
o: resign
rethink
celebrate
disappear
items.why: 처음에는 거절했지만 however 이후 다시 생각해 보는 흐름이에요.

items.q:
What is the writer's main purpose?

Dear residents, from next Monday the main entrance of the apartment complex will be closed for repairs. Please use the side gate on Oak Street until the work is completed in two weeks. We apologize for any inconvenience.
o: To invite residents to a party next Monday
To complain about a very noisy neighbor upstairs
To sell a house on Oak Street
To inform residents about a temporary change
items.why: 공사로 인한 임시 출입구 변경을 알리는 공지예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

It is easy to say you value honesty. The real test comes when telling the truth might cost you something. Only then do we find out whether our words are matched by our ______.
o: actions
clothes
dreams
luck
items.why: 말과 일치하는 것은 행동이라는 의미예요.

items.q:
Read the paragraph and choose the main idea.

People often think shy people dislike company. In fact, many of them enjoy friendship deeply. They simply need more time to feel comfortable and prefer smaller groups to large parties.
o: Large parties are the best place for friendship.
Shyness is a serious illness.
Shy people want company but in a quieter way.
Comfort is impossible for shy people.
items.why: 통념을 뒤집는 In fact 이하에 요지가 있어요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

The teacher's explanation was so ______ that even students who usually struggled with math understood the lesson after hearing it once.
o: confusing
careless
lengthy
clear
items.why: 어려워하던 학생도 이해했으므로 설명이 명확했다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Which sentence is out of place in the passage?

(1) Recycling paper saves trees and energy. (2) A single ton of recycled paper can save many liters of water. (3) Tigers are one of the largest cats in the world. (4) Therefore, putting paper in the right bin is a small action with a large effect.
items.why: (3)은 종이 재활용과 관련이 없어요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

The first chapter of the novel was dull, so I nearly gave up. Surprisingly, by the middle of the book I could not ______; I read until two in the morning.
o: pick it up
write it out
put it down
leave it open
items.why: 시간 가는 줄 모르고 읽었으므로 책을 내려놓을 수 없었다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best title for the passage.

In the past, a letter might take weeks to arrive. Today, a message can cross the world in a second. Yet this speed has created new problems: we expect immediate answers, and silence from a friend can feel like rejection.
o: The Hidden Cost of Instant Messages
Why Letters Are Always Late Today
The History of Postal Workers in Cities
A Guide to Fast Typing on Phones
items.why: 빠른 통신이 가져온 새로운 문제를 다룬 글이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

The mountain path was narrow and covered with ice, so the guide told us to walk slowly and ______ each step carefully.
o: test
skip
admire
forget
items.why: 얼음길에서는 한 걸음씩 조심스럽게 확인해야 해요.

items.q:
Choose the main idea of the paragraph.

When a language disappears, the world loses more than a set of words. Each language carries its own stories, jokes, and ways of describing nature. Once the last speaker is gone, this knowledge is often lost forever.
o: Every language in the world has the same stories.
Speakers of rare languages are always very happy.
A lost language means lost cultural knowledge.
Nature can be described well in only one language.
items.why: 언어 소멸은 문화적 지식의 소멸이라는 것이 요지예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

My brother never keeps his promises. He says he will help, but when the time comes he always finds an excuse. I have learned that his words are ______.
o: worth a great deal
not worth relying on
very easy to forget
always the same as mine
items.why: 약속을 지키지 않으므로 믿을 만하지 못하다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Why did the writer write this text?

The community center is looking for volunteers to read stories to children on Saturday mornings. You do not need teaching experience; you only need a warm voice and a love for books. If you are interested, please contact the front desk.
o: To report a school trip
To review a children's book
To change a Saturday schedule
To ask for volunteers
items.why: 자원봉사자를 구하는 글이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

Nobody expected the small team to win. But with their strong cooperation, they ______ every expert's prediction and took the championship.
o: confirmed
repeated
disproved
approved
items.why: 아무도 예상하지 못한 우승이므로 전문가들의 예측을 뒤집었다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Read the paragraph and choose its main idea.

A well-known study found that people remember the last part of a list better than the middle. For that reason, speakers are advised to put their most important point at the end, and to repeat it briefly.
o: Key points are best placed at the end.
Lists should always be very long and detailed.
The middle of a speech is the most memorable.
Speakers should avoid repeating anything.
items.why: 마지막에 핵심을 놓으라는 조언이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

The café owner did not advertise at all. Instead, she focused on serving excellent coffee, and customers began to tell their friends. Her business grew through ______.
o: sudden luck
newspaper articles
expensive signs
word of mouth
items.why: 광고를 하지 않고 손님들이 친구에게 말해 성장했으므로 입소문이에요.

items.q:
Which sentence does NOT fit the paragraph?

(1) Regular exercise strengthens the heart. (2) It also improves mood by reducing stress. (3) Many people enjoy watching movies on weekends. (4) Even a short walk every day can make a difference.
items.why: (3)은 운동의 효과라는 흐름과 무관해요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

Although the singer was famous around the world, she remained ______ and often thanked her fans for every small kindness.
o: arrogant
humble
careless
lazy
items.why: although 이하의 대조: 유명하지만 겸손했다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best title for the text.

Many children hesitate to ask questions because they fear looking foolish. A good classroom makes asking questions normal, even admired. When questions are welcomed, students think more deeply and the whole class learns.
o: The Foolish Student's Worst Day
Quiet Classrooms Are Always Best
How to Avoid Hard Questions in Class
Why Questions Should Be Welcomed
items.why: 질문을 환영하는 교실의 가치가 요지예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

The designer wanted her chair to be beautiful, but she also knew that nobody would buy a chair that hurts to sit in. In the end, she chose a design that combined beauty with ______.
o: comfort
danger
weight
silence
items.why: 앉기에 아프면 안 되므로 아름다움과 편안함을 결합해요.

items.q:
Choose the sentence that best expresses the main idea.

We often judge a day by its big events, but psychologists find that happiness depends more on small, frequent pleasures: a warm drink, a friendly greeting, a few minutes of sunshine.
o: Only very big events can truly make us happy.
Warm drinks are better than sunshine.
Small daily pleasures matter for happiness.
Psychologists dislike friendly greetings.
items.why: 큰 사건보다 작은 즐거움이 행복에 중요하다는 요지예요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

The road to the village was blocked by snow, and the supplies were running low. The villagers realized that cooperation was no longer a choice but a ______.
o: luxury
mistake
habit
need
items.why: 생존을 위해 협력해야 하므로 필수라는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
What is the purpose of the following message?

I am pleased to recommend Jisoo Han for the student leader position. During the past year, she has organized three school events, helped new students settle in, and always treated others with fairness.
o: To refuse an offer of work
To support a student's application
To announce the results of an election
To describe a school building
items.why: Jisoo를 추천하는 추천서예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

Trees in a forest are not only competitors for sunlight. Their roots connect underground, allowing them to share nutrients with weaker neighbors. In this way, the forest works more like a ______ than a battlefield.
o: factory
desert
team
prison
items.why: 서로 영양분을 나누므로 공동체에 가까워요.

items.q:
Which sentence is unrelated to the others?

(1) Sea turtles return to the beach where they were born to lay eggs. (2) Scientists believe they sense the magnetic field of the Earth. (3) Fresh bread is best eaten on the day it is baked. (4) This remarkable ability helps them cross thousands of kilometers of open water.
items.why: (3)은 바다거북의 귀소 본능과 관련이 없어요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

He spoke in a low voice and chose his words carefully, because the news he had to share was both sad and ______.
o: serious
amusing
ordinary
cheerful
items.why: 슬프고 조심스러운 소식이므로 serious(심각한)가 맞아요.

items.q:
Read the paragraph and choose the main idea.

The idea that geniuses are simply born is attractive, but it is misleading. Studies of great musicians show that nearly all of them practiced thousands of hours, often with the help of dedicated teachers.
o: Teachers are unnecessary for all great musicians.
Talent alone explains every success.
Success depends largely on long practice.
Music is too difficult for most people.
items.why: 통념(타고난 천재)을 뒤집고 연습의 중요성을 말해요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

The company promised to protect the environment, yet it continued to dump waste into the river. Its actions were completely ______ its promises.
o: similar to
contrary to
thanks to
in addition to
items.why: 약속과 행동이 반대이므로 contrary to가 맞아요.

items.q:
Choose the best title for the passage.
