A hundred years ago, a family might have owned only a few books and read them again and again. Now, we have access to millions of titles, yet we read less deeply. Having too many choices can make it harder to focus on any one of them.
o: The Cost of Printing Books
A Family's Favorite Bedtime Stories
Reading in the Dark
When Choices Become Too Many
items.why: 선택지가 많아져서 오히려 집중하기 어렵다는 내용이에요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.

The detective did not believe the suspect's story. Too many details were ______, and the times he mentioned did not match the records.
o: thrilling
decorative
false
friendly
items.why: 시간이 기록과 맞지 않으므로 세부 내용이 사실이 아니라(거짓이라)는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Choose the sentence that best summarizes the paragraph.

Some scientists argue that cities are the greenest places to live. Residents of dense neighborhoods walk more, share walls that save heating energy, and use less land per person than people in widely spread suburbs.
o: Dense cities can use resources well.
Suburbs always use less energy than cities do.
Walking causes cities to grow.
Shared walls make people unhappy.
items.why: 도시의 밀집이 자원 효율을 높인다는 요지예요.

items.q:
Choose the best expression for the blank.

At the beginning of the term, the students were silent and shy. After a month of group projects, they were laughing and sharing ideas, which shows how teamwork can ______ barriers between people.
o: build up
carry on
look after
break down
items.why: 그룹 활동으로 서먹함이 사라졌다는 흐름이에요. break down barriers는 장벽을 허물다예요.

items.q:
Read the paragraph and choose its main idea.

For many years, tomatoes were thought to be poisonous in Europe, and people grew them only as decorations. Over time, bold cooks tried them, and the fruit slowly became a basic ingredient. Our beliefs about food are often shaped by habit rather than fact.
o: Tomatoes are no longer used in cooking in Europe.
Food beliefs can come from habit, not facts.
European cooks have always avoided any new foods.
Decorations are more valuable than fruit.
items.why: 마지막 문장이 요지예요. 음식에 대한 믿음은 사실보다 습관에서 올 수 있어요.

items.good: Not only did she finish the report, but she also helped her teammates.
items.ko: 그녀는 보고서를 끝냈을 뿐만 아니라 팀원들도 도왔어요.
bad: Not only she finished the report, but she also helped her teammates.
Not only did she finished the report, but she also helped her teammates.
Not only she did finish the report, but she also helped her teammates.

cz.st: Not only ___ finish the report, but she also helped her teammates.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 동사가 도치되어 'did + 주어 + 동사원형'이 돼요.

items.good: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
items.ko: 교통 상황을 알았더라면 더 일찍 출발했을 텐데요.
bad: Had I knew about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
Had I known about the traffic, I will leave earlier.
If I would know about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

cz.st: ___ I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

items.rule: if가 생략된 가정법 과거완료는 'Had + 주어 + 과거분사'로 쓰고, 주절은 would have + 과거분사예요.

items.good: The more you practice, the better you become.
bad: The more you practice, the best you become.
The much you practice, the better you become.
The more you practice, the more better you become.

cz.st: The more you practice, the ___ you become.

items.rule: 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급'은 '~할수록 더 ~하다'라는 뜻이에요. 비교급 good → better를 써요.
items.hint: 두 개의 비교급이 짝을 이루는 구문이에요.

items.good: The book that I borrowed from the library was surprisingly funny.
items.ko: 내가 도서관에서 빌린 책은 놀랄 만큼 재미있었어요.
bad: The book that I borrowed it from the library was surprisingly funny.
The book what I borrowed from the library was surprisingly funny.
The book who I borrowed from the library was surprisingly funny.

cz.st: The book ___ I borrowed from the library was surprisingly funny.

items.rule: 사물 선행사를 꾸미는 목적격 관계대명사에는 that(또는 which)을 쓰고, 목적어를 다시 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Despite being tired, he finished the race.
bad: Despite he was tired, he finished the race.
Despite of being tired, he finished the race.
In spite being tired, he finished the race.

cz.st: ___ being tired, he finished the race.

items.rule: Despite(= in spite of) 뒤에는 명사나 동명사가 와요. 'Despite of'나 'In spite' 뒤에 of 없이 쓰는 것은 틀려요.

bad: I wish I am taller.
I wish I will be taller.
I wish I be taller.
items.rule: 현재 사실과 반대되는 소망은 wish 뒤에 과거형(be동사는 were)을 써요.
items.hint: 현재 이루어지지 않은 일을 바라는 표현이에요.

items.good: The results, which were published last week, surprised many scientists.
items.ko: 지난주에 발표된 결과는 많은 과학자를 놀라게 했어요.
bad: The results, that were published last week, surprised many scientists.
The results, what were published last week, surprised many scientists.
The results, who were published last week, surprised many scientists.

cz.st: The results, ___ were published last week, surprised many scientists.

items.rule: 쉼표 뒤에서 부가 설명을 하는 계속적 용법에는 that을 쓸 수 없고, 사물이면 which를 써요.

items.good: It was so cold that we stayed indoors all day.
items.ko: 너무 추워서 우리는 하루 종일 실내에 있었어요.
bad: It was too cold that we stayed indoors all day.
It was so cold what we stayed indoors all day.
It was very cold that we stayed indoors all day.

cz.st: It was ___ cold that we stayed indoors all day.

items.rule: 'so + 형용사 + that ~'은 '너무 ~해서 ...하다'라는 결과를 나타내요. too는 'too ... to'로 써요.

items.good: The bridge was built in 1998 by workers from many countries.
items.ko: 그 다리는 1998년에 여러 나라의 노동자들이 지었어요.
bad: The bridge was build in 1998 by workers from many countries.
The bridge were built in 1998 by workers from many countries.
The bridge built in 1998 by workers from many countries.

cz.st: The bridge ___ built in 1998 by workers from many countries.

items.rule: 수동태는 'be동사 + 과거분사'예요. 주어가 단수이고 과거(in 1998)이므로 was built를 써요.

items.good: Hardly had we reached the station when the train left.
bad: Hardly we had reached the station when the train left.
Hardly have we reached the station when the train left.
Hardly had we reach the station when the train left.

cz.st: Hardly ___ we reached the station when the train left.

items.rule: 'Hardly + had + 주어 + 과거분사 ~ when ...'은 '~하자마자 ...했다'라는 도치 구문이에요.

items.good: I would rather stay home than go out in this rain.
items.ko: 이런 비에 나가느니 차라리 집에 있겠어요.
bad: I would rather staying home than go out in this rain.
I would rather to stay home than go out in this rain.
I would rather stay home than going out in this rain.

cz.st: I would rather ___ home than go out in this rain.

items.rule: 'would rather + 동사원형 + than + 동사원형'은 '~하느니 차라리 ...하겠다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.hint: would rather 뒤의 동사 형태를 생각해 보세요.
